content.title: Screen-in-Screen Montage | Continuous Outer Take, Changing Inner Display
content.summary: Keep one physical display in the foreground and the outer take continuous while only the inner screen changes characters or states. Stable hands, background anchors, parallax, and occlusion prove the same exterior scene; the ending holds the inner result, device, and outer context together.

quick_start.input_format: Physical display + continuous outer take + at least three inner-screen states + independent outer parallax or occlusion + inner and outer final states together
quick_start.recommended_input: In an original nocturnal rainforest lab, a botanist opens a graphite folding thermal monitor. Its screen and bezel stay sharp while wet leaves, amber work lights, and a small team remain softly blurred behind it. Mist and leaves move only in the outer layer; inside the monitor, moth-wing scans, a flower opening, and other readings change in sequence without losing the display boundary. The final inner view gathers frog, moth, flower, and spore readings while the physical monitor, gloves, and same greenhouse remain visible.
required_anchors: Introduce one physical display carrier and clearly separate its inner image from the outer world.
Keep the outer shot continuous with stable device, operator contact and environmental anchors.
Accumulate at least three distinguishable inner states without losing the display boundary.
End with the inner result, physical carrier and outer context readable together.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Keep one physical display in the foreground and the outer take continuous while only the inner screen changes characters or states. Stable hands, background anchors, parallax, and occlusion prove the same exterior scene; the ending holds the inner result, device, and outer context together.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Establish one physical display carrier in a continuous outer shot, keep its bezel, operator contact and surrounding geography visibly stable, and confine every montage cut or state change to the inner screen. Use independent outer-layer parallax or occlusion to keep proving that the exterior take has not cut, then finish by bringing the inner result and the persistent outer context into one readable held relationship.

invariants.rule: Introduce one physical display carrier and clearly separate its inner image from the outer world.
invariants.ablation_failure: An unbounded fullscreen insert removes the screen-within-screen mechanism.

invariants.rule: Keep the outer shot continuous with stable device, operator contact and environmental anchors.
invariants.purpose: Makes inner cuts legible as bounded events.
invariants.ablation_failure: Outer cuts turn the sequence into an ordinary montage.

invariants.rule: Allow meaningful content changes only inside the display while the outer layer supplies independent parallax or occlusion.
invariants.purpose: Proves that the two layers have different temporal rules.
invariants.ablation_failure: Matching both layers shot-for-shot destroys the contrast.

invariants.rule: Accumulate at least three distinguishable inner states without losing the display boundary.
invariants.ablation_failure: One inner clip does not establish a montage system.

invariants.rule: End with the inner result, physical carrier and outer context readable together.
invariants.ablation_failure: Ending on an isolated insert discards the continuous outer proof.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source silver early-2000s MiniDV camcorder
the source nighttime fashion crowd and old stone street
the source party portraits, sunglasses and tan fur coat
the source REC and timecode screen graphics
the source exact inner portrait order and electroclash campaign styling

instantiations.concept: In an original nocturnal rainforest lab, a field botanist holds a rugged folding thermal monitor in one continuous outer shot. Mist, leaves and her gloved hands drift around the sharp device while only its screen cuts among a frog, a moth, a flower opening and airborne spores; the final monitor view gathers all four readings while the same wet greenhouse remains blurred behind it.

instantiations.concept: In stop-motion felt craft, a clockmaker carries a brass diagnostic tablet through one continuous workshop aisle. Hanging gears and wool dust provide outer parallax while the tablet alone switches between four animated mechanism cross-sections; the final cross-section aligns with the unchanged physical clock behind the tablet.
